unit.title: Refranes & Proverbs
unit.subtitle: Reading the folk wisdom natives drop mid-sentence

grammar.title: The sayings that carry a whole argument in one line
grammar.intro: A refrán is a fixed folk proverb — rhythmic, often rhymed, and never taken word-for-word. Educated speakers deploy them to clinch a point or soften advice in a single breath. At C2 you must grasp the literal words, the figurative lesson, and — crucially — when to drop one so it lands naturally rather than sounding like a textbook.

sections.heading: Caution and the safe bet
sections.body: Several classic refranes counsel prudence. Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando — one bird in the hand beats a hundred flying — favours the sure thing. En boca cerrada no entran moscas — flies don't enter a closed mouth — advises silence to avoid trouble. Note the frozen syntax: you never conjugate or rearrange them.
conj: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando
a sure small gain beats a risky bigger one
En boca cerrada no entran moscas
keep quiet and you stay out of trouble

ex.es: Acepta la oferta: más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
ex.en: Take the offer: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

ex.es: No comentes nada en la reunión; en boca cerrada no entran moscas.
ex.en: Don't say a word in the meeting; silence keeps you safe.

sections.heading: Gratitude and silver linings
sections.body: A caballo regalado no le mires el diente — don't inspect a gift horse's teeth — means don't criticize a gift. No hay mal que por bien no venga — there's no bad that doesn't come for some good — is the Spanish “every cloud has a silver lining”, said to comfort after a setback.
conj: A caballo regalado no le mires el diente
don't find fault with a gift
No hay mal que por bien no venga
every cloud has a silver lining

ex.es: El regalo es sencillo, pero a caballo regalado no le mires el diente.
ex.en: The gift is simple, but don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

ex.es: Perdí el vuelo y conocí a mi socio en la sala; no hay mal que por bien no venga.
ex.en: I missed the flight and met my partner in the lounge; every cloud has a silver lining.

sections.heading: Effort, timing and daring
sections.body: A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda — God helps the early riser — rewards diligence, like “the early bird catches the worm”. El que no arriesga no gana — who doesn't risk doesn't win — urges boldness. They pull in opposite directions, so you pick the one that fits your argument.
conj: A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda
the early bird catches the worm
El que no arriesga no gana

ex.es: Empieza a las seis: a quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.
ex.en: Start at six: the early bird catches the worm.

ex.es: Invierte en el proyecto; el que no arriesga no gana.
ex.en: Invest in the project; nothing ventured, nothing gained.

sections.heading: Character and company
sections.body: Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres — tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are — judges a person by their company (“birds of a feather”). Use it to comment, often critically, on someone's associations. Like all refranes, it's delivered whole, as a knowing verdict.

ex.es: Se junta con estafadores… dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres.
ex.en: He hangs out with swindlers… you are the company you keep.

ex.es: Más vale tarde que nunca: al final entregó la tesis.
ex.en: Better late than never: he finally handed in the thesis.

takeaways: Refranes are frozen: never conjugate, translate word-for-word, or rearrange them.
Prudence: ‘más vale pájaro en mano…’ and ‘en boca cerrada…’ counsel the safe, quiet path.
Comfort/gratitude: ‘no hay mal que por bien no venga’ and ‘a caballo regalado…’.
Match the proverb to your argument — ‘a quien madruga…’ and ‘el que no arriesga…’ pull opposite ways.

mistakes.w: Más vale un pájaro en la mano que cien volando.
mistakes.r: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
mistakes.why: The refrán is fixed: no article ‘un/la’, and it's ‘ciento’, not ‘cien’.

mistakes.w: A caballo regalado no le mires los dientes.
mistakes.r: A caballo regalado no le mires el diente.
mistakes.why: The canonical form is singular: ‘el diente’, not ‘los dientes’.

mistakes.w: Al que madruga, Dios lo ayuda.
mistakes.r: A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.
mistakes.why: The set proverb keeps ‘a quien’ and the dative ‘le’: don't swap them for ‘al que … lo’.

exercises.prompt: Te ofrecen un puesto seguro pero modesto. Dirías: “___.”
exercises.prompt_en: You're offered a safe but modest job. You'd say…

options.text: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando
El que no arriesga no gana
A caballo regalado no le mires el diente
En boca cerrada no entran moscas

exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! Prefieres lo seguro → pájaro en mano.
exercises.no: Choosing the safe, sure option is exactly ‘más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando’.

exercises.prompt: Un amigo se lamenta de una desgracia que acabó abriéndole una puerta. Lo consuelas con: “___.”
exercises.prompt_en: A friend laments a misfortune that ended up opening a door. You comfort him with…

options.text: No hay mal que por bien no venga
Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres
A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda

exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Consuelo tras un revés → no hay mal que por bien no venga.
exercises.no: To comfort after a setback that turned out well, use ‘no hay mal que por bien no venga’.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are."
exercises.no: “Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres” — the fixed proverb about the company you keep.

exercises.prompt: En boca ___ no entran moscas: mejor no digas nada.
exercises.prompt_en: A closed mouth catches no flies: better say nothing.
exercises.hint: The mouth must be shut (feminine adjective).
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! En boca cerrada no entran moscas.
exercises.no: The proverb is ‘en boca cerrada no entran moscas’ — the mouth is ‘cerrada’.

exercises.prompt: Match each refrán to its lesson.
pairs: A caballo regalado no le mires el diente
A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda
El que no arriesga no gana

exercises.tts: A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.
accepted: a quien madruga dios le ayuda
exercises.translation: The early bird catches the worm.
exercises.no: It was: “A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.” (the early bird catches the worm).

exercises.scenario: A friend hesitates to launch her business 🚀

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.es: Tengo la idea lista, pero me da miedo invertir mis ahorros.
lines.en: I've got the idea ready, but I'm scared to invest my savings.

options.text: Lánzate: el que no arriesga no gana.
Déjalo: en boca cerrada no entran moscas.
Tranquila: a caballo regalado no le mires el diente.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Para animar a arriesgarse, ese es el refrán.
exercises.no: To encourage her to take the plunge, the fitting proverb is ‘el que no arriesga no gana’.

exercises.say: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
exercises.en: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.”
